risks.description: SDOH factors are systematically underrepresented in most ML training datasets and are inconsistently recorded in EHR systems. Models trained without SDOH representation may perform worse for high-SDOH-burden patients — who are often the highest-need patients in safety-net settings.
mitigationOptions: Flag SDOH gap in monitoring plan.
Stratify performance review by payer mix or neighborhood deprivation index as SDOH proxy.
Engage equity/diversity team to review SDOH risk for this deployment.

content.phaseInNote: Allowable error (% degradation) is separate from these QC limits: it governs how much change is tolerable when a model or configuration changes and sets reject levels for periodic evaluation.

rules.mlTranslation: One control result beyond ±2 SD of the baseline control mean
rules.response: Warning. Inspect with the other rules before acting. No stop.
rules.threshold: ±2 SD (SD measured across baseline control runs)

rules.response: Reject the run. Execute the predetermined response (backup, contingency or hold) and notify the corrective action owner.

rules.mlTranslation: Two consecutive control results beyond 2 SD on the same side
rules.response: Reject. Systematic error: check what changed (model version, prompt, configuration, data pipeline).

rules.mlTranslation: Two consecutive control results more than 4 SD apart, on opposite sides
rules.response: Reject. Random error: inspect components (input handling, tools, sampling settings). Subgroup differences are checked separately (see stratified limits).

rules.mlTranslation: Four consecutive control results beyond 1 SD on the same side
rules.response: Warning by default (reject if the validated rule set says so). Early systematic shift: investigate before it crosses 2 SD.

rules.mlTranslation: Ten consecutive control results on the same side of the baseline mean
rules.response: Reject. Sustained systematic drift: hold, find the cause, and classify the change (re-baseline, verification or revalidation).

rules.mlTranslation: Failed known-answer controls in the last 20 runs, against exact binomial limits from the baseline pass rate
rules.response: Binary results have no distance from the mean, so they are judged as a count. Baseline rate starts provisional and is established with cumulative in-control runs.
rules.threshold: Warn at ~5% false-alarm limit; reject at ~0.3%

rules.mlTranslation: Sensitivity on known-positive controls drops below an absolute floor
rules.note: False-negative bias declared for this use type. The floor is a hard stop, not a warning.
rules.response: Immediate stop. Missed true positives carry the higher harm for this use type. Failover to human review.
rules.threshold: No floor set. The organization must set one; the tool does not supply a default.

rationale: Subgroup flags need a minimum number of cases per subgroup per window before they count; small subgroups are noisy.
Checking many subgroups at once guarantees some false flags by chance. Adjust for the number of comparisons, or confirm a flag on the next window before acting.
Population-stratified control limits serve as the middle path between fixed and adaptive thresholds.
Fixed aggregate thresholds can mask subgroup-specific performance degradation that does not surface until harm occurs.
Fully adaptive thresholds require longitudinal data that is often unavailable at deployment.
Stratified monitoring allows aggregate thresholds to govern overall stop/action decisions while disaggregated tracking provides early warning of differential performance.
Whoever reviews subgroup performance data owns the governance decision about whether differential performance is acceptable — this is not a technical question.

stratifiedGroups.dataRequirement: Local EHR stratification by Age required. If unavailable, flag as monitoring gap.
stratifiedGroups.monitoringRecommendation: Disaggregate monitoring metrics by Age. Flag a subgroup for review when its error rate is at least 1.5 times the aggregate error rate (ratio set at validation; 1.5 is the starting value in the Commons Agent QC Setup) and the lower bound of its 95% interval is above the aggregate rate, confirmed on the next review window. A gap that meets the ratio but not the interval is watched, not acted on.

ownershipStatement.escalationPath: For high-risk use types, corrective actions require co-signature from a clinical governance authority (e.g., CMO, patient safety officer, or equivalent). Single-role sign-off is insufficient.
ownershipStatement.principleStatement: Whoever signs the corrective action owns the governance decision. Threshold values are inputs to that decision, not substitutes for it.
ownershipStatement.statement: The individual who signs the corrective action plan for this deployment is CMIO. This is a governance decision, not a technical one. Threshold values in this tier framework are recommendations — the authority to accept, modify, or reject them rests with CMIO.

rationale: Daily QC runs on known-answer control tasks, the same way a lab runs control material. It does not wait for production outcomes, which often arrive late or never.
Control tasks are built under the approved on-site validation plan, drawn from local cases with verified answers, and run on a fixed schedule.
Production outcomes feed periodic evaluation and lookback, not the daily rules.
Each control result is the model's output on a case whose true answer is known.
For the reject rules on now (1₃ₛ, 2₂ₛ, R₄ₛ, 10ₓ), over a window of 10 control runs:
With no error present, they fire in 6.4% of windows (false rejection).
A 1 SD shift is caught within 10 runs 44.0% of the time; a 2 SD shift 98.6%.

This assumes control results are independent and spread roughly normally around their baseline mean. Scores bunched near a ceiling, or runs that affect each other, can make the real rates different; check the baseline runs before leaning on these.

These are calculated exactly from the rules, not simulated, so they don't change from one protocol to the next. They change only when the rules do, for example when the drift rule switches on after 20 baseline runs.
These are the monitor's own sensitivity and specificity, separate from the model's. Its PPV depends on how often real errors occur: when they are rare, most rejects are false alarms.

Tuning the rule set trades systematic-error detection against random-error detection. Any change to the rule set is a locked-parameter change: logged old → new, re-signed by the independent authority, and the affected controls re-baselined.
Track local prevalence and the model's positive-call rate as monitored metrics in their own right.
PPV and NPV move when prevalence moves, even if the model has not changed. Without this, a prevalence shift reads as model drift.
Validated PPV 35.1% and NPV 97.2% hold only at the prevalence entered; recompute when prevalence changes.

Change control is risk-based and decided in advance, by the system's classification and the type of change (like FDA change control plans and IQCP). Three tiers, used precisely, so routine changes stay proportionate and full revalidation stays rare.

Re-baseline: a new or replaced control item, or a new lot of control material. Establish a new mean and SD for that control only, run alongside the current material; each control has its own chart, so the others are unaffected. No performance claim is re-proven. Signed by the operator.

Verification: the agent changed but its intended use did not (a vendor model version, or a prompt or configuration change within validated scope). Requires the control set and a sample of real tasks, judged against the existing acceptance limits with criteria set in advance; controls alone are only QC. The real-task sample is sized to what the decision needs (larger for this high-risk use), not maximized. Pass: re-baseline and release. Fail: the change does not go live. Signed by the independent authority, because a model change is a locked-parameter change.

Revalidation: the claim changed (new intended use, population, data source or retrieval corpus, or a modification to how the agent works). Spec, acceptance limits, accuracy, precision, subgroup performance and validated range are set again under a new on-site plan. Signed by the independent authority and clinical leadership.
Any change to locked validation parameters (limits, rule set, acceptable cutoffs) is logged old → new and re-signed by the independent authority.
After a reject, re-review only outputs that could cause harm, defined at validation from intended use (worst-case severity and likelihood). Not everything.
Lookback window: from the last acceptable QC run to the hold. If a backup or contingency carried the load, its output during the hold is a second lane.
Misses are the higher-harm error here: prioritize negatives the model issued during the window.
If validation parameters changed during the hold, re-judge past results under the new settings.

Auto-release: results release without human review only when no rejection rule has fired, no warning is past its acknowledgment deadline, the model version is unchanged, and no locked parameter has changed. Acknowledged warnings do not block auto-release.

First response to a rejection: hold, and route the agent's work to the human queue. One automatic rerun is allowed only when random error is suspected; repeated reruns until a run passes conceal real error. Alternatives: fail over to a backup that carries its own QC, or switch to the contingency procedure.

Warnings: set an acknowledgment deadline at validation (starting value in the Commons Agent QC Setup: 1 business day). A warning not acknowledged in time holds the agent like a rejection, with a defined walk-back (escalate, then log).

Human queue: owned by a named role, with a response time set at validation (starting value: the response time staff already meet for the same work; same shift if none is defined). If the owner does not respond in time, the item escalates to a named backup role, then to the independent authority. The same timer applies to every approval in this layer, so nothing waits on one person.

Release authority: the operator may release after a first-line fix (non-analytic cause or clean correction, no failover, no locked parameter changed). Release requires sign-off by CMIO (the independent authority) if the agent failed over, the cause was not found, a rerun failed, or a locked parameter changed during the hold. The person who loosened a limit does not also release under it.
Corrected outputs: decide at validation who is told when a released output is found wrong, and how (clinician, patient, chart correction). Fixing the agent does not fix outputs already acted on.

Contingency: time on the manual procedure is monitored, with escalating reminders at intervals set at validation (starting value: 24 hours, 72 hours, 7 days), so contingency does not become the permanent workflow.

A failure the QC missed triggers a QC design review, not an automatic new control: were the controls at the right decision points, and were the rules strong enough for the method's sigma? Move or replace a control before adding one. Size the set by decision points: one control near each boundary that matters, plus a few anchors and drift sensors. Each added control adds false alarms.

Outward reporting: confirmed failures go to the vendor and the organization's safety event reporting; optionally to the Commons Peer Challenge Registry once registration reopens (it is browse-only while paused), until a standard registry exists.
Repeat-run precision: the same inputs can give different outputs. Run a fixed case set several times and measure the spread, rather than inferring precision from one validation run.
Baselines from thin data start provisional and are established with cumulative in-control runs; flagged runs never feed the baseline.

content.note: These terms decide whether you can monitor it yourself and react to updates. They matter more since HTI-5 removed the federal model-card requirement for certified EHRs.
Each trigger leads to one of three tiers (see Change Control in Section 4): re-baseline, verification or revalidation. Not every change is a revalidation.
triggers: Vendor model version change → verification (control set plus a real-task sample; independent authority signs)
Prompt or configuration change within validated scope → verification
New or replaced control item, or new control lot → re-baseline of that control (operator signs)
Change to intended use, patient population, data source or retrieval corpus → revalidation (independent authority and clinical leadership sign)
Monitoring rejection or sustained drift → hold and corrective action; once the cause is found, classify the change into one of the tiers above
Change in clinical workflow, merger or reorganization → review, then classify into a tier
Additional site-specific trigger: [not defined — complete before deployment]
